hero.alt: Green title card reading Reading Quran on Your Phone Without Wudu

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 183 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Prophet recited the last ten verses of Al Imran after waking, before making wudu; chapter on reciting after hadath.

sources.title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 146 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Prophet recited in all conditions except when junub; jurists named hold reciting without wudu is allowed but reading from the mushaf requires purity.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 373 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: The Prophet remembered Allah at all times.

sources.title: Qur'an 56:77-80 (Surah Al-Waqi'ah) on Quran.com
sources.supports: Text of the verses describing the Quran in a well-preserved Record touched by none except the purified.

sources.title: Qur'an 56:79 on Quran.com
sources.supports: Clear Quran translation renders the purified as angels.

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham fatwa 05038: touching the phone screen when reading Quran without wudhu
sources.supports: Touching a phone screen displaying the Quran does not require wudu; pixels behind glass are not permanent writing; recommends staying in wudu.

review.notes: Re-read every capture retrieved 2026-10-29. The phone-screen ruling is attributed only to Darul Ifta Birmingham (a Hanafi fatwa body), not stated as universal; the fatwa's recommendation to stay in wudu is included. The mushaf-purity view is attributed to the jurists named by at-Tirmidhi in the Arabic note under hadith 146, and the 56:79 angels interpretation is disclosed rather than used to derive a ruling. Menstruation is flagged as a scholarly difference without a ruling and deferred to the existing guide. Muwatta Malik 15/1 returned HTTP 403 and IslamQA is not an approved domain; neither is cited. Distinct from the existing can-you-read-quran-without-wudu page by focusing on phone use and linking to it. Hero generated locally with the meadow palette and inspected: 1200x630 legible title card, not duplicated in body. No app CTA; links /quran, /prayer-times and existing wudu, ghusl and what-breaks-wudu guides.

claim_checks.claim: Prophet recited the last ten verses of Al Imran on waking before making wudu
claim_checks.explanation: 'He then, recited the last ten verses of Sura Al-Imran, got up and went to a hanging water-skin. He then Performed the ablution'; chapter: recitation of Quran after hadath.

claim_checks.claim: Prophet recited the Quran in all conditions as long as he was not junub
claim_checks.explanation: 'Allah's Messenger would recite the Qur'an in all conditions, as long as he was not Junub.'

claim_checks.claim: Sufyan ath-Thawri, ash-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq held one may recite without wudu but read from the mushaf only while pure
claim_checks.explanation: Arabic note: qalu yaqra'u ar-rajulu al-Qur'ana 'ala ghayri wudu' wa la yaqra'u fi al-mushafi illa wa huwa tahir; wa bihi yaqulu Sufyan ath-Thawri wa ash-Shafi'i wa Ahmad wa Ishaq.

claim_checks.claim: The Prophet remembered Allah at all times
claim_checks.explanation: 'The Apostle of Allah used to remember Allah at all moments.'

claim_checks.claim: Touching a phone screen showing the Quran does not require wudu, because pixels behind glass are not permanent writing; staying in wudu is still recommended
claim_checks.explanation: 'it will be permissible to touch the screen without wudhu when the Quran app is displayed'; mentions pixels and glass shield; 'A believer should however always be in the state of wudhu even though it may not be necessary.'

claim_checks.claim: 56:79 says touched by none except the purified, rendered in the Clear Quran as angels
